description.narrative: Catchment management, policy formulation, planning and implementation at Meso and Macro levels are strengthened

Micro level: The direct participants of the project are the population in the water catchment areas of Lokere and Lokok in the districts of Moroto (approx. 100,000 people), Napak (approx. 45,000 people) and Kotido (approx. 250,000 people). Meso-level: The direct target group consists of 1,070 people, including representatives of the watershed management organization, which is made up of research institutes, the private sector, religious and cultural institutions, civil society organizations, political and technical authorities of the districts, and the decentralized legal institutions. These persons will be trained in the further implementation of the management plans for the Lokok and Lokere river basins.Macro-level: The direct target group will be around 80 people, in particular from the MWE as well as from other line ministries such as the MAAIF, the Ministry of Equality, Labour and Social Development (MGLSD) and the Ministry of Local Government. At the macro level, universities/research institutions, the private sector and WASH networks such as UWASNET and the Uganda WASH Agenda for Change Forum are also involved.Indirect participants include approximately 810,000 people living in the Lokok and Lokere catchment areas where the project is being implemented, as well as an estimated 45 million people in Uganda's four water management zones who will benefit from the project-supported policy reforms to protect water sources.

The overall goal of the project is to strengthen the management of watersheds in Uganda through policy reforms and their implementation at the national level.Specific objectives-The management of the watersheds in Uganda is strengthened through political reforms and their implementation at the national level (meso and macro level).-Improve the resilience and livelihoods of communities in the Lokere and Lokok catchment areas (micro and meso level).
